extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys/respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state professional discipline, including notice, response, scope of exclusion, publication, and reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis for reciprocal exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the exclusion of Respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office is ordered for violation of the ethical standards set out in 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and 10.23(b) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59. The USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by a state disciplinary authority unless grounds under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) justify otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to contest (40-day response requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must inform the respondent and direct that if the respondent seeks to contest imposition of exclusion pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order is mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address provided under 37 C.F.R. § 11.11. Delivery shown by USPS records supports the Office's determination that notice was given. Failure to file a timely response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for finding a 'genuine issue of material fact' under 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must present information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline would be unwarranted based on any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not timely produce such information, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue and impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state's discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified misconduct grounds supporting exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice states that the respondent was disbarred by the state for 'failing to safeguard clients' funds, failing to provide proper accounting to clients, engaging in dishonest conduct, and failing to notify clients of his suspension from the practice of law.' These types of misconduct support exclusion under the referenced ethics rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misconduct demonstrating failure to safeguard client funds, inadequate client accounting, dishonesty, or failure to notify clients of suspension are substantive bases for reciprocal discipline under USPTO rules (via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23 provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion (practice limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office, beginning on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion prevents the respondent from practicing before the USPTO in all patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until reinstated consistent with USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations while excluded (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order grants limited recognition only as needed to permit compliance with 11.58(b) (see limited recognition entry); otherwise the excluded practitioner must follow the duties and client-notice/file-transfer obligations imposed by § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance (30-day limited practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is strictly time-limited (30 days here) and limited in purpose (to comply with § 11.58(b) obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO, and shall not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and the reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public. Disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is governed by the requirements of § 11.60; the respondent must satisfy those regulatory conditions to be allowed to practice again before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and proof of mailing requirements (certificate of service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; a certificate of service documents that mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of mailing and delivery (e.g., USPS records showing delivery) supports the Office's position that notice was properly given and can be dispositive when a respondent fails to file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of respondent's failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has not filed a response to the Notice and Order; accordingly, it is determined that: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) exclusion from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to contest within the required period permits the Office to enter final reciprocal discipline without further factual development; timely, substantive response is necessary to raise an issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Official Gazette notice (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the respondent (name, registration number), state the exclusion from practice before the USPTO, cite the ethics rules violated (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a),(b) via 10.23(c)(5)), describe the underlying state discipline and the misconduct (e.g., failing to safeguard client funds, failing to provide proper accounting, dishonest conduct, failure to notify clients), and state the effective date of the state disbarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice is the public record of the exclusion and must accurately summarize the reasons and authorities for the discipline.
